summary.intent: Use the GSD manager workflow to drive the v2.0 CipherBox milestone to completion: plan/execute/verify/ship phases 76, 78, 79 via parallel background worktree agents, discuss and scope Phase 78 (infra-independent recovery tool), triage the pending-todo backlog into closeout phases 80-83, and begin discussing/planning Phase 80.
summary.outcome: Phases 76, 78, and 79 were all planned, executed, verified, hardened via reviewer findings, and shipped/merged (PRs #610, #611, #613, plus workflow-improvement PR #614); a todo-triage PR (#612) retired 6 resolved todos and added closeout phases 80-83 to the ROADMAP; Phase 80 was fully discussed (locking a significant sharing-crypto scope expansion around recipient-pubkey pinning) and its CONTEXT.md was committed, with background planning about to be dispatched when the transcript ends.

repo: GSD background planner/executor agents committed to worktrees may land on either the ephemeral `worktree-agent-*` branch or the canonical `feat/{slug}` branch depending on whether the GSD commit helper's first commit triggers a branch switch — always verify which branch received the commits before deciding whether to re-home or just push.
`EnterWorktree` refuses a repo-root→worktree switch on this host, so resumed/verify/ship agents must operate via `git -C <worktree>` / absolute paths instead of cd-ing into the worktree.
GSD commit helper can report `commit_failed` as a false negative even though the commit landed — verify with `git log` before retrying.

ROADMAP.md conflicts between parallel phase branches are typically 'both sides true' (each phase completed independently) and should be resolved by keeping both sides; STATE.md conflicts are branch-local bookkeeping and can be resolved with `git checkout --ours`.

`pr-release-preview.yml` triggers on `[opened, synchronize, reopened, labeled, unlabeled]` so it fires even for draft PRs; CodeRabbit's `.coderabbit.yaml` has `drafts: false` so it skips draft PRs — enables a draft→wait-for-release-bot→mark-ready ship flow to avoid CodeRabbit reviewing a stale head.

D-07 naming is ambiguous in this repo: there are two unrelated 'D-07's — the Rust/FUSE write-plane(UUID)/read-plane(ipnsName) invariant (already enforced) vs. the web/SDK import boundary ESLint rule (the actual open item, anchored to `2026-07-06-d07-boundary-eslint-rule` todo and `68.2-SECURITY.md`).

Recipient-pubkey trust model gap: share issuance correctly binds the pasted recipient pubkey client-side, but every re-mint/reconcile/upgrade consumer (Rust `rotation_deps.rs`, TS `owner-reconcile.ts`, web `owner-reconcile.service.ts`/`ShareDialog.tsx`) re-fetches `recipient_public_key` from `/shares/sent` and trusts the server's round-trip value — a compromised relay could swap it to retain access after a scope-exit rotation.

ECIES-wrapped `encryptedReadKey` blobs cannot be used to verify/recover the recipient pubkey without the recipient's private key, so pinning must store the pubkey separately at issuance (in the owner-sealed `NodeWriteBody`), not derive it from the wrapped blob.
`initialize_vault` (Rust) mints fresh random root keys on every call, so a fail-closed vault-init retry must ECIES-decrypt-and-resume the existing key blob rather than re-mint (Phase 76 landmine).

code.finding: `collect_sent_shares()` calls GET /shares/sent and returns the stored recipient_public_key per share — this is the untrusted server round-trip that Phase 80's D-03 pin is meant to guard against.

`wrap_key(new_read_key, &grant.recipient_public_key)` wraps the freshly rotated read key to whatever pubkey the server just returned in step 7, with no comparison against the originally pasted pubkey.

Recipient pubkey is pasted by the owner out-of-band (`hexToBytes` at line 179) and used to client-side ECIES-wrap the item read key (`wrapKey` at line 184) — this is the trustworthy issuance-time binding that later round-trips get compared against under Phase 80's fix.

`lookupUser(pubkey)` only confirms a registered user has the pasted pubkey via `findOne({where:{publicKey}})` — server does not choose or supply the recipient key at issuance, it merely validates existence.

workflow: Establish the pattern once and reuse it: plan/execute/verify/ship agents each run in an isolation worktree, `git checkout feat/<slug>` first (since plan/execute artifacts live on the phase branch, not main), and the orchestrator handles push/re-home/conflict-resolution afterward.
Serialize ship pipelines (or at least their SDK-E2E gate) across phases sharing infra (Postgres, :3000 API bind) to avoid state corruption from concurrent runs.
When two parallel background executors exhaust API quota mid-run, resume in their existing worktrees (not fresh ones) to preserve atomic partial commits and installed node_modules/deps.

Distinguish resumable failures (transient API errors, quota) from non-resumable ones (agent explicitly stopped by user) — SendMessage-based resume only works for the former; the system refuses to resume a user-stopped agent.

When a bookkeeping-only conflict (ROADMAP/STATE) recurs across many rebase-replay commits, switch from `git rebase` to a single `git merge --no-edit main` to resolve the conflict once instead of N times.

For genuinely gray-area architectural decisions surfaced mid-discussion (e.g. recipient-pubkey trust), trace the actual code end-to-end (issuance vs. re-mint vs. reconcile) rather than reasoning abstractly — this is what correctly escalated a 'closeout' phase into a real crypto design decision.

Before committing to a workflow file change (e.g. ship-phase.md draft-PR flow), verify the underlying CI/bot trigger conditions in their actual config files (pr-release-preview.yml triggers, .coderabbit.yaml drafts setting) rather than assuming.

friction: Two parallel background executors (Phase 76, Phase 79) both exhausted the session's API quota mid-run, requiring detection, worktree-state assessment, and manual resume.

`EnterWorktree` repo-root→worktree refusal repeatedly forced agents to fall back to inline `git -C`/absolute-path operation, skipping the formal Skill-driven pipeline (e.g. Phase 76's resume skipped the formal `gsd-verifier` pass, requiring a separate verify dispatch later).

The 76 ship agent initially misreported CI as fully green while the Windows Cargo check was actually failing — caught only because the user pushed back; root cause was a test-only bug (non-UUID child_id in the ported D-07 test).
A background CI-watch/monitor process died along with its parent agent when quota hit, requiring the ship agent to be resumed and to poll CodeRabbit inline instead.

A quota-resume cron scheduled for 5:55am fired but only delivered a prompt for the orchestrator to act on rather than autonomously continuing — user noted it 'did not even do' what was needed, so it was removed.

The user accidentally stopped the Phase 78 ship agent mid-pipeline ('trying to get back to the main session'); the system would not allow resuming that specific stopped agent, forcing the orchestrator to do the remaining mechanical conflict-resolution inline instead.

A background fix agent for Greptile findings died on a transient 'Connection closed mid-response' API error partway through implementation with substantial uncommitted work, requiring careful assessment before resuming.

Repeated recurring ROADMAP.md/STATE.md merge conflicts every time a phase branch needed to catch up with main after another phase merged — pure bookkeeping noise requiring manual resolution each time.
A transient DNS failure ('Could not resolve host') caused a `git push` to fail once and required a retry.
open_items: Log a `recovery-tool-large-file-verified-assembly` todo for the deferred availability gap: large (>256KiB) dag-pb file bodies won't recover via the Phase 78 recovery tool on gateways that serve `/ipfs/` but lack the trustless `?format=raw` API; the verified-assembled-fallback (recompute UnixFS root CID from assembled bytes) was deliberately deferred as unvalidatable offline against Kubo's DAG layout.
Phase 80 planning (background worktree dispatch, re-homing to `feat/rotation-write-plane-and-re-mint-durability`) was about to be launched when the transcript ends — not yet completed.
Phases 81 (TEE Republish & IPNS-Record Correctness), 82 (Wire-Encoding Domain Hardening), and 83 (Desktop Resilience) are defined in the ROADMAP but not yet discussed or planned.

A v2.1 backlog was documented in ROADMAP.md but not yet turned into actual phases: web freshness/a11y/observability polish (C3), ops/CI hygiene chores (C5), Tier-3 large-file refactor (#6), and three defer-forever features (ERC-1271 contract-wallet auth, CRDT IPNS inbox sharing, alternative MFA factor types).

Phase 80's D-03 (recipient-pubkey pinning) requires a metadata-schema change to `NodeWriteBody` following `METADATA_EVOLUTION_PROTOCOL`/`METADATA_SCHEMAS` with Rust/TS CBOR parity, plus updates across ShareDialog issuance/upgrade, web+TS owner-reconcile, Rust+TS rotation engines, and recovery-tool ignore-unknown-field tolerance — all still to be planned/implemented.
23 pending todos remain in `.planning/todos/pending/` after the closeout triage (6 retired, 4 partial with residue), not all of which map to phases 80-83 or the v2.1 backlog explicitly.
